events.title: Micipsa dies
events.text: King Micipsa, son of Masinissa, dies at Cirta and leaves Numidia jointly to his sons Adherbal and Hiempsal and his adopted nephew Jugurtha.

events.title: The three heirs
events.text: At their first council, Hiempsal pointedly refuses Jugurtha the seat of honour and proposes cancelling Micipsa's last decrees.

events.title: Murder at Thirmida
events.text: Jugurtha's men break into a house at Thirmida, a town whose site is lost, and kill Hiempsal.

events.title: Adherbal defeated
events.text: Jugurtha routs Adherbal's army; Adherbal flees to the Roman province and on to Rome.

events.title: The kingdom divided
events.text: A Senate commission led by Lucius Opimius splits Numidia: the richer west to Jugurtha, the east with Cirta to Adherbal.

events.title: Raids on the east
events.text: Jugurtha raids Adherbal's lands to provoke a war he can blame on his cousin.

events.title: Battle near Cirta
events.text: Jugurtha's night attack scatters Adherbal's army; Adherbal escapes into Cirta with Italian traders defending the walls.

events.title: Siege of Cirta
events.text: Jugurtha rings the gorge-bound city with ditches and towers; two Roman embassies come and go without effect.

events.title: Scaurus at Utica
events.text: The senior senator Marcus Aemilius Scaurus summons Jugurtha to the Roman province, but leaves without lifting the siege.

events.title: Cirta surrenders
events.text: Urged by the Italians, Adherbal surrenders on a promise of his life; Jugurtha has him tortured to death.

events.title: Massacre at Cirta
events.text: Jugurtha's troops kill the grown men of Cirta, among them the Italian merchants, and Rome's people demand war.

events.title: Bestia's war
events.text: The consul Lucius Calpurnius Bestia lands in Africa and takes several Numidian towns.

events.title: Peace bought
events.text: Jugurtha surrenders thirty elephants, cattle, horses and a little silver for a lenient peace, after bribing Bestia and Scaurus.

events.title: Albinus in Africa
events.text: The consul Spurius Postumius Albinus renews the war but achieves little and returns to Rome for the elections.

events.title: Disaster at Suthul
events.text: Aulus Albinus marches on Jugurtha's treasure town; lured away, his camp is stormed and his army sent under the yoke.

events.title: Metellus arrives
events.text: The consul Quintus Caecilius Metellus restores discipline in the demoralised army.

events.title: Vaga garrisoned
events.text: Metellus places a garrison in Vaga, a market town full of Italian traders.

events.title: Battle of the Muthul
events.text: Jugurtha ambushes Metellus by the river Muthul; the legions hold and the Numidians scatter.

events.title: Siege of Zama
events.text: Metellus storms the walls of Zama for days and fails, then winters in the Roman province.

events.title: Vaga rises
events.text: On a feast day the people of Vaga massacre the Roman garrison; Metellus retakes the town in two days.

events.title: Bomilcar's plot
events.text: Jugurtha's confidant Bomilcar plots to hand him over; the plot is discovered and Bomilcar executed.

events.title: March to Thala
events.text: Metellus crosses fifty miles of desert with water in skins to reach Jugurtha's refuge at Thala.

events.title: Thala falls
events.text: After a forty-day siege the deserters inside burn the palace and themselves; Jugurtha has already fled with his treasure.

events.title: Among the Gaetulians
events.text: Jugurtha raises and drills a new army among the nomad Gaetulians of the steppe.

events.title: Alliance with Bocchus
events.text: Jugurtha wins over his kinsman by marriage Bocchus, king of Mauretania, to join the war against Rome.

events.title: Cirta occupied
events.text: Metellus holds Cirta, where he keeps his booty, prisoners and baggage.

events.title: Marius takes command
events.text: Gaius Marius, elected consul and given Numidia by a vote of the people, lands with recruits from Rome's poor.

events.title: Metellus recalled
events.text: Superseded by his former officer, Metellus leaves Africa bitter; he later celebrates a triumph as Numidicus.

events.title: March on Capsa
events.text: Marius drives cattle for food and marches by night across dry country to surprise the oasis town of Capsa.

events.title: Capsa destroyed
events.text: Capsa opens its gates; Marius burns the town, kills its adult men and sells the rest into slavery.

events.title: The rock fortress
events.text: Far west near the river Muluccha, a soldier climbing for snails finds a path, and Marius storms Jugurtha's mountain treasury.

events.title: Sulla arrives
events.text: The young quaestor Lucius Cornelius Sulla joins Marius with a strong force of cavalry from Italy.

events.title: Ambush on the march
events.text: Jugurtha and Bocchus fall on Marius's army at dusk as it marches east to winter quarters; the Romans hold a hill through the night.

events.title: Second battle near Cirta
events.text: Near Cirta the two kings attack again and are routed; Bocchus begins to seek terms.

events.title: Sulla's mission
events.text: Sulla rides through the desert to Bocchus's court with a small escort to negotiate.

events.title: Jugurtha betrayed
events.text: Bocchus lures Jugurtha to a parley, his escort is cut down, and he is handed in chains to Sulla.

events.title: Reward for Bocchus
events.text: Bocchus keeps western Numidia, the old kingdom of Syphax around Siga, as Rome's friend and ally.

events.title: Numidia for Gauda
events.text: Rome keeps Numidia a client kingdom; it soon passes to Gauda, Jugurtha's sickly half-brother.

chartNote: Share of the area of modern Algeria (its present-day provinces), by the power that held most of each province. A simplification: ancient sources give no boundary lines, the 116 BC partition and the 105 BC cession to Mauretania are known only in outline, and Roman control meant the towns and roads its armies held. The vast Saharan provinces, outside any kingdom, dominate the shares.
